findings.summary: The migrate case statement's default (failure) branch dropped `failed=$((failed + 1))`, which the pre-diff code had. Now a migrate call that returns anything other than 201/409 (e.g. a 500 from Gitea, or a suppressed network failure that leaves status empty) prints a '! FAILED' line but never increments $failed. The end-of-run summary ('created=... skipped=... failed=...') under-reports, and `[[ "$failed" -eq 0 ]] || exit 1` at the end of the script exits 0 even though repos failed to mirror. For an unattended nightly cron job whose entire purpose is reliable backup, this silently masks failures from anything watching the exit code.

findings.summary: gh_api's curl call has no --max-time (unlike gitea_api, which got --max-time 1800/60 with a comment explaining the bound). The brief asks to 'bound how long any single request can run' — gh_api is used in the paginated GitHub enumeration loop and can still hang indefinitely on a stalled connection to api.github.com, only partially satisfying that requirement.
